title: Add compact RAG probekit, tool-proxy patterns, and local debugging walkthrough
author: Sofia Liang
release_notes: Introduces a compact RAG probekit for local debugging, plus tool-proxy pattern examples; non-breaking; docs and quickstarts added.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams building RAG-enabled features often need compact, reproducible playbooks for validating tool-calling behavior, network boundary issues, and observability probes that can run locally or in CI. This PR introduces a lightweight "probekit" with example tool-proxy adapters and a step-by-step debugging walkthrough for common failure modes (authorization failures, streaming disconnects, prefix cache cold starts). The goal is to reduce onboarding time for engineers experimenting with tool-calling agents and to provide a small set of deterministic smoke scenarios used by internal and external quickstarts.

What this PR does: Adds a compact RAG probekit (playkit/) that includes: a) minimal HTTP tool-proxy (tool-proxy/) that simulates third-party connectors and supports configurable failure modes and latency; b) a set of two RAG sample agents (agents/basic-prober, agents/flow-proxy) demonstrating tool-calls, structured output validation, and streaming resume; c) an authoring guide (docs/quickstarts/probekit.md) with a local-run recipe, test assertions, and CI smoke integration; d) small SDK usage examples (examples/ts and examples/py) showing typed tool contracts.

Backward compatibility and security: This PR is additive and marked non-breaking. The tool-proxy is explicitly opt-in for examples and quickstarts; no production-facing API changes were made. All secrets in samples are placeholders; README includes guidance to use KMS-backed secrets in production scenarios.
